summary: Bradford's transit positions span TTC reliability, safety, congestion, transit expansion, and active transportation. Bradford has consistently advocated for a TTC 15-minute money-back service guarantee (DSKkoPtDZFM, DSIfzz2jjCo, DRhNrDEDKmt), platform edge doors, police presence, and cleanliness/lighting standards through a "Safer TTC" motion (DWZyuhICoQQ, DVhJtcuD2D5). Bradford has pressed for Scarborough/Eglinton East LRT funding parity with the Waterfront East LRT (DXc5lIFjQo_, DW9omxgiiuh) and supports transit separated from car traffic (DUbXa8rClRC). On congestion, Bradford backs a Congestion Relief Commissioner (Cth_Y8zAPV0, DIPfGv-yL6S), opposes ride-share caps (CyWIsi2gS-6, DDIZpJfyQQA), and has proposed reopening King Street to vehicles during streetcar suspensions (DLYR_Fru6ru). On cycling, Bradford supports "safe and sensible" bike lanes built case-by-case with community consultation (DBrZ4Ogytu6, DBMivFtSg_w), and has championed Destination Danforth and Bike Share expansion (CNYbaD7Bj9U, CBN92ZVhLYb).

key_positions.stance: Supports a 15-minute TTC money-back service guarantee that refunds fares for delays of 15 minutes or more, modeled on GO Transit, London, and Washington DC.
Supports installing platform edge doors at every TTC subway station, along with police presence and cleanliness/lighting standards.
Supports advancing the Eglinton East / Scarborough LRT and argues Scarborough has been left behind on transit funding compared to the Downtown Waterfront LRT.
Supports rapid transit physically separated from car traffic, citing Finch West LRT as an example of failure when transit shares the road.
Supports appointing a Congestion Relief Commissioner / Traffic Czar with accountability for reducing Toronto traffic.
Opposes caps on ride-share (Uber/Lyft) vehicles, arguing they raise prices and wait times and reduce options where transit is insufficient.
Supports bike lanes built case-by-case with genuine community consultation; opposes processes lacking engagement (e.g., Bloor West) and supports adjusting lanes that are not working.
Supports active transportation expansion including Destination Danforth, ActiveTO, and Bike Share Toronto growth.
Opposes the RapidTO permanent reconfiguration of Bathurst/Dufferin, supporting only a time-limited World Cup pilot following the 2015 Pan Am model.
Supports reopening King Street to personal vehicles while streetcars are diverted due to construction.
Supports continuous transit expansion (subway, LRT, higher-order transit) by all levels of government, citing decades of underbuilding.
Supports electrifying the TTC bus fleet and moving toward a zero-emissions fleet by 2040.
Supports bus priority lanes/RapidTO corridors to improve service for transit-dependent communities.
